In addition to these attacks that they carried out once got their units out in the way that we just described, at the same time they were launching attacks with all kinds of weaponry from that part of the inner-city of Sarajevo that was held under their control?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Because a considerable part of the inner-city of Sarajevo; that is to say, Grbavica, Hrasno, Dobrinja, Nedzarici was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I would add Ilidza and Vogosca. All of that is an integral part of Sarajevo. Rajlovac, too. Yes, that was under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: As parts of the town of Sarajevo; that is to say, all of these municipality, like Ilidza, Vogosca, Rajlovac were in fact municipalities of the city of Sarajevo, and different neighbourhoods were linked up; that is to say, there were no strict separation. For example, Ilidza, in fact, was linked to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll get to that, but we have to look at the map. At this point in time you have answered my question, yes, or rather, you have made the Chamber aware of this. Now I would like to deal with documents, Mr. Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a 65 ter document here, 00603. There is a translation, of course, so could this document please be placed on the monitors. That is a document dated the 26th of December, 1994. Could we please have page 2 displayed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You see it says here underneath this document: "Colonel Dragicevic," and then underneath that there is some explanation in relation to who it was that signed this. Can you please explain how this document was created, and could you tell us whether it is an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Could it please be enlarged, and could we start from the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Page 1. Do you see it? Is says, "Commander of the SRK organ for MV and PP." Can you explain that, first?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but could it please be enlarged a bit because I can't see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask that -- well, yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Those first few paragraphs, I'm actually interested in the first two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see them now, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So the "Command of the SRK and the MV and PP organ."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The organ for morale, religious, and legal affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 26th of December, 1994. That's a month after you arrived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Here it says, "Urgent instructions on how to proceed."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: First paragraph: "On it's 24th of December, 1994 at 1.200 hours, a cease-fire agreement between the warring parties entered into force. With regard to this, focus your activities on the following." Is that correct? Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Explain to military and command personnel that it is in our interest to fully respect this agreement and not to bring its implementation into question by our acts and activities, meaning that we should not hinder, impede, and slow down the activities of the state and army leadership aimed at establishing peace." Is that the way it was?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now move on to page 2, so that I don't read the rest of it. Could you tell me how this document was created, and who signed this? Did you give any instructions with regard to that? Was this done with your consent?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course, with my consent. But I think -- well, I can't see this, this thing down here. I can't see what it says, what is written here, but there is no doubt about that. This is a document of my organ, or rather, the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this 65 ter document, 00603, be admitted into evidence because it does have a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Registrar, number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D137, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, already at that moment when you signed this at the end of December, you were aware and you had been informed by the security services that people, or rather, the leadership of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had already started well in advance preparations for an offensive that was supposed to come in spring or summer. Is that right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: We had received information from intelligence organs, but every experienced, professional officer knew that a major offensive was being prepared. Based on everything that was going on in the previous period, we knew exactly that every cease-fire that had been signed by the commands or their political leaderships, of the army of BH that is, were only used to prepare new offensive activities. It was not the case only now. It was done in the previous period but now in particular. So, yes, we did know. We didn't know the date when it would start, but we knew that something like that was being prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me, since you were under sanctions, international sanctions and sanctions imposed by the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia since you did not have food or enough weaponry, can you tell me did you not pay great attention not to do anything in the period that was to ensue that would jeopardise your own position? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Our position was such that the only thing that suited us was peace; that is to say, without any kind of combat activities. That was our operations position and the general position of the units of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. We were totally, completely without any reserves, especially in terms of large calibre ammunition, we only had some scant reserves in the brigades. The corps itself did not have its own reserves, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that in this period of time; that is to say, especially when you arrived, that you made every effort not ever to launch any offensives; whereas, offensives and attacks were permanently being launched from that part of Sarajevo, the inner-city of Sarajevo that was under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. That situation made it incumbent for us not to take any kind of measures that would turn out to be counterproductive; that is to say, that in this situation what suited us was to have peace so that we would somehow try to improve our situation, especially in terms of supplying units with basic supplies and equipment that was needed for combat activities, because we knew what kind of offensive awaited us in the coming period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that in this period of time from December until April; that is to say, December 1994 until April 1995, there were permanent attacks from the part of Sarajevo that was under BH army control, and there was random shooting from moving objects? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We knew that they were using these mobile platforms on which they would usual place artillery pieces of larger calibres. They would shoot from or fire from one position and then quickly mover to another position. In order to cause counteractivities, they used localities that they were not supposed to use; that is to say, hospitals and other important localities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now we have another document, 65 ter 02297.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have it shown to the witness on the screen. It's been translated and it's very short.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You can see it here. Is this a document issued by the SRC command information centre-press centre dated 11th of April, 1995? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to ask you this. First confirm what I asked you; the 11th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the bottom at who signed it. It says, "Assistant commander for MV and PP, Colonel Dragicevic." Did you personally sign it, or did one sign it on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: This was signed on my behalf by the head of the legal department who normally stood in for me, so everything is in order with this document. It was done with -- on the basis of authorisation as he was given permission to sign a document of this nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In this document, one can see that this is an instruction on information of public on VRS general staff information system. And what do these abbreviations stand for, ISGS VRS?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: This is an instruction on how to inform the public by the information service of the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 1: "Muslims violated the agreement on cessation of hostilities." Is that what says here?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Item number 2 "The offensive has taken many victims on Muslim side." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "VRS forces hold the defensive lines with a firm hand."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "UNPROFOR has sided in the conflict."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "We do not carry out combat operations and we do not violate the agreement."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And there is a note: "Strictly bear in mind the above mentioned instructions when preparing information from the war front." Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you stand by what's written here. Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, definitely. This is the information we received from our superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you abided and adhered to the cessation of hostilities? You held defence lines; and everything you did, you did in order not to violate the agreement? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can document 65 ter 02297 be given a number, because there's a translation provided?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Harhoff would like to put a question to you, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We will certainly admit this document. But I would like you to ask the witness if he with explain the meaning of point number 4 in the instruction: "The UNPROFOR," it says in point number 4, "has sided in the conflict." Does the witness know what this refers to?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to take this into consideration with respect. Witness, can you explain to Chamber what this UNPROFOR sided in the conflict means, and we're talking about the 11th of April, 1995?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: It is not directly related to there specific date. That's the date when the instruction was received with relation to something that was happening in the previous period, that is failure to undertake any punitive action with regard to the incident on Dobrovoljacka Street, the passive attitude of UNPROFOR with regard to the building of tunnel under the airway of the airport, the tunnel being used by the BH army to commute and communicate, and a number of other indicators. One of the conclusions was that UNPROFOR has sided -- had sided with the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have this document 02297, please be tendered as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is will become D138.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, and Your Honour Judge Harhoff, in order to explain in more detail about what you asked you, I have a document here, 65 ter 00257, and I decided to discuss it as well. Can we please have this document displayed on the witness's monitor. It's another brief document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can see that this document is dated the 27th of May, and this order apparently seemed to be issued by General Major Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I asked you a minute ago and you gave an explanation to me, but most of all to the Chamber, that the VRS units did not breach the rules of the total exclusion zone throughout the whole period that you spent there; that is, until April and May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: However, when you -- once you realised that the BH offensive was imminent, you had to think about the possibility of any way taking some of the heavy weaponry placed under the protection of UNPROFOR in view of the imminent situation?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That was the idea. But in view of the gravity of our situation, we had to take measures in order not to be tricked with respect to the return of our weapons in case an offensive would be launched. In other words, we want to prevent this from being too late. The corps was adapted for very quick action and adaptation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you counsel. The answer given by the witness seems to trigger another question about the lack of ability on the UNPROFOR side to control the activities of the BiH army, and my question is this: Was, in the witness's opinion, was the UNPROFOR mandated to take punitive measures against UNPROFOR -- sorry. Was UNPROFOR mandated with the authority to take punitive measures against violations committed by the BiH army or by the Serbian army, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is perhaps the crucial issue in this case that you are going to render a definitive ruling.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you know that UNPROFOR had found itself in this position and this role, precisely in order to prevent violations of total exclusion zone agreement by any party involved; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to the agreement, that should have been the case; however, the practice was something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Not a single violation of the total exclusion zone was committed -- that was committed by the BH army was ever punished by NATO air-strikes? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. Or rather there were never punished for breach of the agreement by the NATO air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Harhoff, this is precisely the reason why I put this document to the witness in order to address this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I understand. But the document seems to be about securing of the taken UNPROFOR checkpoints and not so much, as I can see here, about violations of the exclusion zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try by way of questions to gain the answer that you precisely ought to be interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that as soon as the VRS took over a number of heavy weapons on the 25th and 26th of May, it was immediately bombed, even though the VRS did not use these weapons in any operation at all? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in Pale and other positions of the VRS were bombed on the 25th and 26th of May? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but most of all ammunition, weapons, and food depots and storage facilitates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And only after that did this order -- was there order issued and formulated as it reads here. I'm going to read it out to you. It was issued on the 27th of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the instruction was to carry out this order in the spirit contained in this document, and everything else that is written here. You can read it for yourself, and you confirm that this order is related to the bombing of the 25th and the 26th.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Probably, this precipitated this kind of order, presumably. That was a direct cause.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the reason that you were at the time convinced that UNPROFOR sided with the BH army, because immediately after the weapons had been taken over without it being used at all NATO intervened and bombed with their air force?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like this document, 00257, to be tendered as Defence evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I show that 65 ter number 00257 is already Prosecution Exhibit, P396.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My oversight but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Whiting, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, P396.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, what do you have to say? What do you suggest?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I withdraw my proposal for it to be tendered into evidence as Defence exhibit. It's sufficient, and we have our own perception of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. We have -- we can't have it tendered twice. We need to check the numbers. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give our evaluation of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, after these strikes of the 25th and the 26th May, the BH army was encouraged and launched more and more offensive operations? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We construed this based on our military assessment that this was a prelude to what we knew was coming, and that is a fierce offensive that they were planning to launch.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that even before June, there were offensive operations, vehement attacks launched by the BH army that you had to respond to?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, especially on the outside front line, Nisic, Trnovo, et cetera, there were constant combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can the witness please be shown document, 65 ter 02447, since it's a 65 ter document and there is a translation of it existing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You can see this document. The SRC command, number 20/05-189, dated 16th June 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And it's signed by the assistant commander, Colonel Luka Dragicevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This document contains information and report of the Sarajevo offensive?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: About the beginning of the offensive, by joint forces of the BH army against the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that in this offensive, not only the 1st Corps but rather the 3rd and 7th and other corps took part, and at that time it was a massive offensive on all front lines with ten times the stronger manpower of the BH army? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But not only stronger in terms of manpower, number of attackers, but in every other aspect, except, of course, what later turned out to be true: We were better organised, and our morale was at a high level. Our combatants and fighters knew what they were protecting, and they knew that they had to sacrifice their lives in order to defend their families and their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you the first paragraph. Just a few things in order to move faster. That on that day, on the 15th of June, at 3.00 in the morning, the Muslim forces carried out an all-out attack at all sections of the front line with stronger artillery and mortar support? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And further on it says that the corps units were ready for the onslaught of the enemy on all parts of the front, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then in the next paragraph: "With regard to the strengths of the troops engaged and width of the front of the attack, it can be concluded that it was the commencement of the long ago announced Muslim offensive."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then further down: "According to reliable information, the Muslims, despite the losses sustained and unrealised tasks during the 15th of June, they continued -- continued with the attack in the days to come. "And that Muslims also go for the option that our units not saving mortar and artillery ammunition during the first days of combat activities in such a way that they would be left without artillery support." Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this 65 ter document, 02447, please be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will become D139.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now we have a document that the Prosecutor already introduced today as P491, and the 65 ter number is 2456, and the date of the document is the 18th of June. This document is one that you signed as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please -- yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, yet again, if we could lift it up a bit, the document, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So here it is. Again, it has to do with information concerning the Sarajevo front; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now it says here in the first paragraph: "In spite of losses sustained and further on during the course of the day as well, the enemy was desperately and fiercely attacking all lines of Defence and shed shells on our positions, barracks, and units and corps and civilian settlements." Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And in the third paragraph: "Until now, the fiercest attack was launched yesterday on the positions." Could you please help me with this?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The Igman Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "The Igman Infantry Brigade, Zanik, Vala, Kokoska, where around 2.000 tank, artillery, and mortar projectiles landed." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Then in the next paragraph you say at that moment you had information that 14 of your soldiers were killed and 42 were wounded, 13 of which seriously. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, yes. This was a document that was already tendered by the Prosecutor, so it's a Prosecution Exhibit. So, of course, I'm not insisting on us tendering it as well. There is no need really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number is P491. In order for the transcript to reflect it, I need that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, further on in June and July, this offensive, including attacks, took place every day? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So then it was not as intensive in August, but there were attacks in August, too?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of far lesser intensity. Quite simply, this was the time that was required to carry out some preparations and probably changes in tactics in order to move on to the next stage of the offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have a document SRK, of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, which has not been translated, and its date is the 17th, or rather, the 27th of August, 1995. In relation to that, since the date is the 27th of August, 1995, I would just like to put one paragraph to the witness. The document is DD00-1897. Out of a series of documents, I selected this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And what is it, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a combat report for that day that was signed by the then deputy of Dragomir Milosevic, because Dragomir Milosevic was on sick-leave in Belgrade. And this has to do with very intensive activity on the part of the BH army on that day, on the 27th of August, that is. Many civilian neighbourhoods were targeted.. Actually, perhaps I don't even have to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to ask the witness whether on the 27th of August, in terms of helicopter sorties and these activities, did you feel that a preparation -- that an offensive was being prepared by Sarajevo or in Sarajevo on the 27th of August?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it further down here in this document. If the forward command post is being taken, that means that something forceful is to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, I don't really have to show this document, and I don't have to tender it. I don't even have to ask to have it marked for identification be. At any the rate, you can say that on day, according to intelligence information, you noticed that in Sarajevo something was going on, as if a new offensive was being prepared?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The document probably says so, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, I don't mean to do any bean counting here, but you have already had an hour and eight minutes for your cross-examination -- no, you've had an hour and 38 minutes and you have 22 minutes left to finish your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I just out of fairness want to be clear about where we stand at the moment with respect to time. We learned this morning and I informed the Defence, and I believe we sent an e-mail your legal officer, that one of our witnesses for this week is ill and unable to travel. I don't want to refer to him by name because he has protective measures. It is 114 who is scheduled to be either last or next to last for the week. In addition, we are not planning -- we were not planning to start the next witness until tomorrow, because we thought this witness was to going to take the entire day and the next witness will not be ready until tomorrow. I just want that to be clear. I do anticipate some redirect examination, maybe ten or 15 minutes at the most, maybe 15 minutes, but I thought that should be put on the record for Your Honours to consider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting. As far as we can see, the Defence still has roughly half an hour left of its cross-examination and that will bring us to the break or, in fact, we will have the break before the Defence will complete its cross-examination. The Chamber also has a number of questions to put to the witness after the cross-examination and the redirect. So I'm sure we will find good use of our time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, really, I had the intention of asking you in view of the importance of this witness and the documents, the documents I have -- the documents, I wanted to ask for an extension of time to a maximum, because I have these very important subjects to deal with and I have not even touched on them yet. And all of the questions I did put so far were important ones, so I really should be allowed to examine this witness properly. Time should be observed, but we should also observe matters that are of crucial importance, because I cannot do a thing in 20 minutes only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, in light of the explanation provided by the Prosecutor, and of the information regarding our next witness, we may give you some extra time. But I would like to draw your attention to the fact that you must try and be as short as possible, but be as you succinct as you can be in relation to the indictment this particular witness and make sure that we are able to finish within the allotted time frame. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, if you can really, whenever possible, just give me yes or no answers, please.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I have a document. The 65 ter number is 02550. If you have a look at it down here, it is yet again a document that you stand by; however, under the authority given to you. Is that right? I mean, it bears your signature? .

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see the signature, but my first name and last name are printed out there. But if I read this document out, if I see what the content is, there will be no problem. However, could I see it from the very begin, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is dated the 25th of July, 1995. I'm going to read out this big paragraph here, the one that says: "Based on intelligence information and serious complications in relations with UNPROFOR forces which aim at provoking our forces fire in order to ask for the intervention of rapid deployment forces and NATO air-strikes and with the aim to secure strict control of fire of our forces, to eliminate unnecessary, negative, or even catastrophic consequences." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that even at the moment, when there was strong mutual shelling primarily from the Muslim side, in your responses you prohibited any kind of action to be taken vis-a-vis places were UNPROFOR was. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But let's go back to civilians. You know that when you came, the anti-sniper agreement was in force?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I was made aware of that agreement that was in force, and this agreement had a been signed earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that during your period, so to speak, great attention was paid to that, to not violating this agreement. And in this period up until April, there were practically no violations of this agreement?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can claim with responsibility that on our side maximum efforts were made to fully observe every agreement that was signed. That was the case while I was there, and that is what did happen indeed in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: We can say that that was the period when on the 12th of March, those two little girls were killed in Grbavica by sniper fire; is that right? In March, remember? Remember two little girls of Serbia ethnicity were killed by sniper fire?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: There were civilian fatalities, unfortunately. In most cases, they were children.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: On both sides. They are the least cautious of all, and that is probably the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we say that you, on your side, were aware of these actions, particularly during the Muslim offensive where there was certain intensity of shelling on one side and another intensity on the other, that civilian casualties could not have been avoided? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, most often, especially in densely populated areas when there is fighting between two parties, the victims and the casualties are civilians. It was evident not only in Sarajevo, that applies to all wars, especially civil wars. Civilians are always the ones who suffer most casualties in terms of number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that on the territory under the VRS control, there were lots of casualties among soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: There were also many casualties among civilians?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this 65 ter document, 02550, please be tendered as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Tapuskovic, this document seems to be an order from the VRS leadership to prevent fire on the UNPROFOR forces, and I'm not sure of the meaning of the last part of the order as we can see here on the first page. It says that a decision on a possible activity against the UN forces, if found in an apparent suspicious or provocative mission or activity, is to be made by the commander of the SRC, or the operative team of the SRK command. Could you ask the witness to clarify the meaning of this last paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, you took a firm position not to launch any activities against UNPROFOR, and you never took that course? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: However, in the situation where there was the heaviest possible fighting, you issued an additional warning to avoid any mistaken or circumstantial fire being opened in the vicinity of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: That was a standing order. Occasional orders just reinforced this order or amended it, if the previous practice imposed some new approach to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did the BH army often carry out actions precisely in the vicinity of UNPROFOR in order for a certain shell to hit UNPROFOR forces as a kind of response fire?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: We had this kind of --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object. This is not the first time this has happened, but it's the first time I'm objecting. I'm not sure what the foundation is for the witness to be able to speak about that, to offer any kind of opinion about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: That was -- that would have been my question in extension of the witness's answer. Could you ask the witness directly if the accused, General Milosevic, ever issued any order to -- to strike against UNPROFOR forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask a very direct question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know very well that neither General Milosevic nor anyone else from the VRS had ever issued any order to act against UNPROFOR soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps commander or for that matter any member of the command or commands of the subordinate units within the corps did issue any kind of order of that nature, nor did I ever read anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: One might say that the major danger of hitting UNPROFOR was due to the fact that the BH army often fired from the vicinity of UNPROFOR positions?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Their main and basic tactics was to open fire from the locations close to the -- these positions that could be punishable or presented in the media as the doing of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. We had information that they were firing from nearby UNPROFOR and UNMO, I think it's called, positions, as well as other vital facilities such as hospital, cultural and religious buildings, and et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... Very well. I think it is now time to have a break. I think the parties can ponder this question and we shall get back to it afterwards. It is now 23 minutes past 12, and we shall resume at 12.43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Mr. Tapuskovic, before letting you proceed, Judge Harhoff would like to have some clarification about the question he asked before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. The question I wanted to put to the witness was in relation to the order which the Chamber has before it on the screen. It appears to be an order possibly signed by the accused - I cannot see the signature - but the important thing about the contents is in point number 2 of the order, which as I quoted before, says that attacks against UN forces can be ordered if the UN forces acts suspiciously or provocatively. And my question to the witness, and I would just like to you answer yes or no, is if General Milosevic or anyone acting under his command every issued such an order. Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I do, yes. As far as I know, in order to attack UNPROFOR, forces has ever been issued --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Has never been issued.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would start now with a few topics that I have left through most of my time, and I would deal with the ten documents that have been entered with my approval when they were tendered by the Prosecution. I would focus on 65 ter 2522. That's the information about crime trends in the month of July. That's Prosecution Exhibit 484.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, can we say that all these dozen or so reports were identical in one aspect. If we look on page 4 of the B/C/S version and page 5 of the English version of this report relating to the month of July, and if we look at item 2, international law of war, it says here as follows: "No criminal reports for this type of crime were filed in this reporting period." Is this what it says here?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When talking about international laws of war, in all ten reports, it says that no criminal reports were filed for violations of the international law of war.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I already said that I never heard or read anything about any kind of violations of that nature committed by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. I haven't seen all of these documents though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What I mean to ask you is this: As Defence counsel for Dragomir Milosevic, I'm particularly interested in the period that you were there and about which you can give direct evidence. Let me ask you this. It is a straightforward question. You know very well that in the area of responsibility of the SRC and the territory under its control, in the south itself; that is to say, Grbavica, Hrasno, Dobrinja, Nedzarici, Ilidza, Lukavica, not a single war crime was committed in these areas?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of, and my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we also say that the same applies to the general area, including Ilijas and Vogosca and elsewhere? Is that fair to say, too?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that in these areas there were no camps, yes or no, for civilian or any kind of detainees?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that detainees, members of the BH army, were not maltreated and most of them were exchanged? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: They were under the jurisdiction of security organs, but I never heard of any single incident of maltreatment, nor did I read about it and heard about it at command briefing sessions, and most of them, as you said, were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now concerning civilians --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, there seems to be so sort of contradiction between the two answers just given by the witness. In the English transcript, the witness confirmed that there were no camps. And in the second answer, he then says that the detainees in the camp were not maltreated. How is the Chamber to understand this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, then, it's badly translated. I said that captured members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were always exchanged and none of them was ever tortured or experienced any hardships and unpleasantness, but were, rather, exchanged for those captured by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There was no mistreatment or killing of the captured Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I never heard of anything of that nature happening in the area of responsibility of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that not a single civilian, even if there were Muslims and Croats in the area of responsibility, were mistreated or killed outside of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that for the relevant period, while I held this post.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that, therefore, no criminal report could have been filed for any war crime in the territory in inside the city and in other places under the control of the SRC?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: If these things didn't happen, then no criminal reports could have been filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now go back to the period when this heavy shelling took place between the two parties that you mentioned earlier. Can we say that in a conflict of that nature, it is only to be expected that both of civilians and the casualties on both sides would be sustained?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going object to the kind of broad nature of these questions and the lack of foundation. I mean, you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, you've heard the Prosecutor. Can you rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I do appreciate the Prosecutor's reaction, but the Chamber should evaluate whether there is anything inadmissible in my question. I don't understand the objection put forth by my learned colleague, Mr. Whiting. I asked in amid this heavy shelling exchange, it is only to be expected that casualties will be sustained by both sides, both in among civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, was that something that was inevitable?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In war conditions and during an offensive, were you able to investigate anything whether -- about what was happening on the other side, in order to institute proceedings against anyone? Was it possible at all in war to carry out any kind of -- investigation while there were shellings landed on -- landing on both sides?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: There were no conditions for anything like that in the territory under the control the SRC, and there was absolutely no possibility to conduct any investigation in the opponent's territory. Even in more quiet times, it was impossible to do because there was an explicit prohibition issued by the highest leadership of BH barring any Serb from entering their territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In a war of that kind, was it possible at all to trace someone and prosecute him when the front line was over 200 kilometres long? Was anything of that kind possible?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: During such fierce offensives that was ongoing at the time, that was a life-and-death situation, there was no possibility of that sort, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, I'm getting worried. I'm looking at the clock. How much more time do you need to complete your cross-examination? How many more minutes would you like?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will do me best to complete it in 20, or maybe 15 minutes. I am aware that I have overstepped my time-limit, but I think can I finish by 1.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1.15. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: My last question relating to this topic is this: You were not able to investigate the cause of death of civilians in the territory under your control. The only thing you could do was to just bury them. You did not conduct investigations, did you?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. We were not even able to bury them peacefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is a mistake -- no, no. 65 ter 02550 has not been entered, although I have requested it to be tendered and admitted as -- into evidence. That's 65 ter 02550.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Mr. Tapuskovic. I remember now. Mr. Registrar, please give us a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be admitted as Exhibit D140.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please explain to the Chamber a few things about this map that you see behind you. Can you please just turn around so that you can answer my questions and look at it. You may have seen this map. This is the map made by Commander Major-General Milosevic and approved by Major-General Ratko Mladic. Do you recognise this map?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show to me and explain to the Chamber where the separation lines were and how long they were? Can you confirm that they were over 200 kilometres long?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: May I stand up?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please stand up, and then afterwards you will explain to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: These are separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe you can do it sitting down. So can you confirm that these blue lines were the ones held by units of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that it was over 200 kilometres altogether including those lines?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The overall line, separation line was certainly over 200 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In your day, in view of the existence of this tunnel that did you know about, when units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, primarily the 1st Corps, would get out through that tunnel, who was in a worse situation then? Can one actually talk about a siege imposed on anyone, or who was under siege then?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Siege is a term, if I can put it that way, that was promoted by the media and generally accepted. So no one can really talk about any kind of siege. You can see this full well on the map. You can see the position, as I have already said, that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps was in. It was unbearable from an operations point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: When BH army units would go out that you tunnel and would take up these blue linings, isn't it Ilijas and Ilidza that is under siege, and there Nisic plateau up there as well?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, you can see it on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The existence of this tunnel fully eliminated the concept of any kind of siege?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And if we're talking about hills within the blue line, were all hills above under BH army control, except for the viewpoint at Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: From Ilijas, Ilidza, or from the Nisic plateau, in order to get to Lukavica where the command is, especially when there were wounded persons involved, wasn't that something which absolutely exposed people to even greater danger, the danger of losing one's life. Can you show the Trial Chamber what road this is, say, from Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if I will be able to do it technically speaking in view of the headphones that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just please don't say anything for a moment and just go up to the map and show us what this is, but just don't cover the map with your back. So Ilidza, where is Ilidza?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So which one way does one have to go? Is this 90 kilometres away from Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness without a microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To get to Lukavica, well, it depended on the weather and other things related to possible firing at those roads. In the summer, about two or three hours would be needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you show the Nisic plateau? Is it up there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was it under siege of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Was Ilidza under siege by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Where is Ilidza -- no not Ilidza, Ilijas? If you could please confirm in the microphone?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was Grbavica fully encircled as well? Show us.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot see very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But do you know?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I lived in Sarajevo. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, sit down and give us answers. Was Nedzarici encircled?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Nedzarici, no, not totally, but - how should I put this? - almost totally encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: At any rate, can we say that the separation lines in the inner-city of Sarajevo were always at the foot of the mountains or hills?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the foot of the mountains and the hills that are in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was Vogosca underneath Zuc and Hum?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, there's this other topic, and then I'd like to conclude. You are an air force man?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I assume that you know what air bombs are.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What is their regular purpose? I mean, they are a permissible military weapon.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of the air force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You know that the representatives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the representatives of the army of Republika Srpska both had air bombs?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Everybody had the same type of weaponry, more or less, depending on the depots that were under their control, from the beginning of the war, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now answer a few questions in relation to Prosecutor's Exhibit 188, in terms of 65 ter. Of course, it has been translated, so 188 is actually a 65 ter number. Here it is. Please look at page 2 for a moment, if we can just have it shown for a second. Can you tell us who it is that signed this? Yes. It says verified by on behalf of the commander Major Mile Radic, and you will see here on the left, isn't that right, commander Major-General Dragomir Milosevic, right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: But I would like to see this in B/C/S is it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can we move on to page 1 now, please. See, this is a document dated 19th of April, 1995. That is the time when you knew that this offensive of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was being prepared?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We knew before this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. You see what it says here under very urgent, order on full combat readiness for all SRK units. Could you explain that, briefly please?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Full combat readiness means that all units should be totally ready for rapidly going into action, or rather, repelling attacks. I mean the soldiers who are on furlough or who are doing something else, too. Also weaponry artillery pieces that the positions should be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. See, is says in the next paragraph, "We have information indicating that the enemy is preparing actions and planning activities against the forces of the corps. In order to thwart and intentions, I hereby order." Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then there is a series of orders; for example, the Defence line are to be met to the maximum, crews and teams are to be positioned by their weapons, take positions and be ready act instantaneously. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Personnel in barracks should be well rested and prepared to respond." This is an a bit further down; and then it says, "air bombs and launching pads should also be ready," right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Should be ready," and everything else it says here,"to take possible action if there is an attack by the other side." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to repeat all of that. It is clearly state what had it is what. I have to finish. But it says at the end here: "Check to see whether any drunken soldiers or officers; and if there are some such persons, they should be detained straight away." If at the very end of the document, and if necessary, we can deal with that -- well, actually, we're not going to use up the remaining two minutes, but this is what we can show at the very end, if you would please turn to page 2. And let me read out two more thing from the very end. "Duty to take all necessary measures in order to prevent attacks by the enemy." It's towards the end. Can you see that? And it says further on: "When engaging the enemy fire, only a targets you can see in order to avoid unnecessary waste of ammunition." It's towards the end, the fifth paragraph from the bottom?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Right? That's what I have read out to you. That's what it says?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And then it was insisted here on some occasions -- well, let me say this: Check that there are no drunken soldiers or officers; if such are found, put them in prison immediately?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: "Such measures and instructions can no longer be changed without proper authority."

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So that means that you can only use the resources you have available only if you are attacked. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. I wish to thank you, Your Honours, and the witness, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic, for your cooperation. I shall now give the floor to Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I begin, I wonder if Defence counsel wants to put the last document into evidence. I don't believe it's in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My omission. 65 ter number is 188. I would have like to have it admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be admitted as Exhibit D141, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Whiting for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Colonel, can you tell us when you arrived in The Hague for your testimony here?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yesterday, on Sunday, did you have occasion to meet with me and with other members of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Afterwards did you also have occasion to meet with members of the Defence team to discuss your testimony?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, in your cross-examination, you testified - it's at page 34 - that after Dragomir Milosevic was treated in Belgrade for his eye injury, that he returned to his command post on the 10th of September, 1995. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you mean "probably"? Did he or didn't he?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, no, he did return, but perhaps, you know, the date. Well, if that is what the document says, then that is the way it was. I don't really remember dates. I just read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. But approximately at that time your memory is that he returned to the command post.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you resume command?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You also said that the -- he cut short his leave after the NATO air-strikes; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When he resumed command, did -- was he informed about the events that led up to the NATO air-strikes?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that was the case, but just let me explain something to you. The corps commander as soon as he enters the zone, the area of responsibility that is under his command, he in fact assumes his role as commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But I was focussed on a different point. You assume that he-- you testified that he cut short his leave as a result of the NATO air-strikes. And so is it based on that you assume that he was informed of the events that led up to those strikes when he resumed command, or do you have other knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you say --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: What did you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The question has to do whether or not he was informed when he resumed command about the events has led up to the NATO air-strikes? And I believe you answered just a moment ago that you assume he was. Why do you assume that? That's based on what?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: It is only natural. It is it a matter of course as far as the military is concerned that the commander has to be aware of what was going on in the previous period and he should be informed about this directly about the -- by this from -- by the person who stood in for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know who stood in for him?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The Chief of Staff of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You testified at page 45 of the cross-examination that the ABiH had superiority in terms of number of persons but also weapons. Are you sure about that answer, that the ABiH had superiority in terms of weapons?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: In terms of the concrete situation that was evolving during the offensive, I'm sure about that. And I am even more sure of the quantity of ammunitions and shells and other things that they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your answer is limited to the offensive that occurred in the middle of June of 1995. That's what you were talking about when you gave that answer?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It was obvious then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How -- did that offensive last more than a couple of days?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, more than a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was the ABiH successful in that offensive or were they repelled by the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The army of Republika Srpska carried out its task with full success. That to say, the members of the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What do you mean by "full success," in terms of whether the offensive was repelled? Was the offensive stopped or not?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The offensive was stopped and the main task that the corps had before them were carried out. That is to say, it maintained most of the territory, its own personnel levels and the population that it was duty-bound to defend.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You testified at page 45 of the transcript that the VRS strictly adhered to the heavy weapon exclusion zone. Did UNPROFOR share this opinion, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what UNPROFOR felt and thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On May 24th of 1995, did the Bosnian Serb army remove weapons from the Weapons Collection Points?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to this question, a full answer. If I had some documents, maybe that would help refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, if they had, would that have been a violation of the total exclusion zone?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, depending what the agreement stipulates, i.e., in which situation the weapons are to be returned or rather, placed under the control of the party that had handed in the weapons. I don't know the details thereof, but in any case, it would be only normal to return the weapons if one of the parties is threatened by fierce offensive, and it was common knowledge that such an offensive was in the offing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you are not aware of the details of the agreement, and you are not aware of events that occurred on May 24th, for example, then on what basis did you give your opinion that the VRS strictly adhered to the exclusion zone?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Based on all the documents at our disposal or rather that I had opportunity to see as well as on the basis of all the collegium meetings and briefings and discussions with lower ranking commands when we visited these units as well as other information. That's the crux of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you aware -- do you know anything about an ultimatum that was given by Sir Rupert Smith on the 24th of May to the VRS to re-establish the exclusion zone? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No. I know of no such document. Generally speaking, I know there were such cases. However, I didn't have any document or order relating to this concrete incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I'm not speaking at this moment about a document. Were you aware of an ultimatum that came from General Smith on or about that date?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Therefore, if you remind me in some other manner, but at this juncture I just cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, you testified in cross-examination and I don't -- I don't recall difficulty on this subject but you testified on cross-examination that there were NATO air-strikes at that time. Do you recall testifying about that? NATO air-strikes occurring on the 25th or 26th of May and that the ammunition depot in Pale was bombed. Do you remember testimony to that effect?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's what happened and I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question then. Do you have any knowledge about a ultimatum that came before those air-strikes by NATO, or do you know nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I personally don't know in what form and to whom this ultimatum was issued, whether it was to the command of Sarajevo-Romanija Corps or to someone else. I don't know anything about it. I just can't remember this minute anything specifically about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I'm just going to press a little bit here on this question because of the way you answered the question. Is it that you don't remember anything about this topic at all or you don't remember specifics?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why I should be aware of the ultimatum. If there was one, those in charge in the command were aware of that. Those who cooperated with UNPROFOR. The only thing we could have received about this was a piece of information on an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Colonel, I am going to ask if you could please focus on my question and try to answer the question. Do you know anything about an ultimatum that came before the NATO air-strikes or not. It's a simple question. Do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I already responded to that. I cannot remember any specific the about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember anything general about it, anything at all?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: About what?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: An ultimatum from NATO before the air-strikes occurred. Do you remember anything at all, whether general, specific, anything at all about it.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Not now. But I probably knew something -- had I probably known something, of, I would have remembered. It's been a long time ago. I truly don't remember anything about that or any role of mine in relation to this ultimatum.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's fine. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If we could look, please, at Prosecution Exhibit 396, which was discussed during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, this is following -- I said I would move on, but it's actually on a related topic, events that occurred in the following days in May. And this order which you discussed on cross-examination, it says -- it is talking about -- if we could just blow up, yeah. Thank you. It is talking about UNPROFOR checkpoints which have been taken by SRK forces. Can you tell me why UNPROFOR checkpoints taken by SRK forces? What was the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what the direct cause was, but I know what the general situation was and what awaited us, and there is probably a direct relation and cause to all this, but I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In your mind, does the taking of UNPROFOR checkpoints constitute an attack on UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily. The taking can be performed in various ways. I don't know how it actually happened in this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And could you explain to us in what way would a taking of an UNPROFOR checkpoint not be an attack.

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Well, in my view, and that's how I see it, an attack during a war, if carried out with weapons and produces certain combat activity, and something is taken or captured by means of this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's a taking that is an attack. Can you give -- are you able to give an example of how a checkpoint, an UNPROFOR checkpoint could be taken and it not be an attack?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I said that I don't know how this was carried out in this particular case, in what way. I know nothing about that. This is an order which shows that some of the checkpoints of UNPROFOR have been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know anything about UN hostages, personnel of UNPROFOR being taken hostage by the SRK or forces of the SRK on the 26th of May 1995, at this exact time? Do you know anything about that subject?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I know that there were hostages, or rather, that UNPROFOR members were, in military terms, captured and this was done on orders by the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you say "the superior command," what command are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And would such orders be communicated through the corps command of the SRK down to the forces on the ground?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's mandatory. As soon as you receive an order from a superior command, it specifies how this particular task is to be carried out and who will carry it out, whether it's going to be the corps command or some other unit than the level to which this order is forwarded works out the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would like some clarification about this question that has just been put you by the Prosecutor. A while ago my colleague, Judge Harhoff, asked you if in the event that General Milosevic or his subordinates had given an order with a view to action being under taken against UNPROFOR, and your answer was to say never. Now, as regards a question that was put to you by the Prosecutor regarding hostage taking, you said that the decision had undoubtedly been taken by the Main Staff of the SRK, but that this had been communicated by the standard and usual chain of command. Don't you see that there is a slight contradiction here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
