utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. I'd like to be cited precisely. I don't think that this is what I said, because it is contradictory. If an order reached from a higher level, then lower levels were supposed to carry it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you are saying that the accused or his subordinates handed down orders which hinted at measures to be taken against UNPROFOR but that these orders came from above?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Because communications with the highest level of UNPROFOR command were maintained as well as cooperation the highest command organs of the VRS, which in this case was the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. Whiting, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Does -- did the taking of hostages, of UNPROFOR hostages, constitute an attack on UNPROFOR, in your mind?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Depends on the specific circumstances that it was carried out. If it was done under threat or during fire, I see that as an attack. However, there were liaison officers who explained directly to UNPROFOR why something was being done, why things were happening, that there was no need for any clashes and fire being opened at each other, and how problems can be solved in a more dignified and normal way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tapuskovic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection to the Trial Chamber, but it was Mr. Whiting who raised this issue for the first time. I must say that in view of what Dragomir Milosevic is accused of, I think this is irrelevant. It may be a subject to certain evaluation. However, as far as the indictment is concerned, it is irrelevant, and therefore I object to this question. He has not been accused of this in the indictment at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Whiting, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that the Defence opened the door to these kinds of questions because they spoke specifically about the events at the end of May and the NATO air-strikes which this is connected to, and, secondly, they raised in cross-examination the witness spoke specifically about the attitude towards UNPROFOR and attacks on UNPROFOR. There is a document that went in about attacks on UNPROFOR and specific statements were made. If they were relative on cross-examination, they are relevant on redirect examination. And this was a topic thoroughly explored on cross-examination, and I have a right to explore it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite right, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Colonel, were the UNPROFOR hostages ever mistreated, to your knowledge, of course?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they weren't, at least I don't know of any one of them being hurt. They may only have suffered some psychological consequences as a result of fear, but I have no knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were they -- were any of the hostages chained to targets, potential targets, within VRS territory? Do you have any knowledge of that?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: I heard about that in the media, but I myself didn't see anything like that. It could possibly be the case, but then again it may not. I personally didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Two questions to follow on from that. First of all, if -- would hearing about such a thing in the media be a sufficient basis to refer the event for criminal investigation?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Second question is: Is -- was the taking of the UN hostages consistent with the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: No, it was not in accordance with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was there any referral made by any commander, including the corps commander of the SRK, to investigate that -- the taking of the UN hostages as a possible violation of the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: The corps commander carried out the order he received from his superior officer in relation to these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: In other words, it was not him who gave this order but, rather, carried the order received from his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: My question again: Did any commander, including the corps command of the SRK, initiate any steps to commence an investigation of the taking of the UN hostages as a possible violation of the international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: LUKA DRAGICEVIC
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Whiting, you don't have much time left, two minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going -- I have a number of topics to cover, and I think given the length of the cross-examination and the topics that were covered I'm going to ask for additional time and that we have the witness again tomorrow to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: This is why I exactly take the floor because we have one more minute to go, and we should not overexploit the patience of the interpreters and the staff. The Chamber, too, has a few questions, so it may be that we shall have to call you back, Mr. Witness, tomorrow morning for not too long time because we have another witness. But let me just confer with my President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I don't think I would be any longer than 15 or 20 minutes, and I believe we have sitting in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Whiting, we had planned to have two witnesses today. We only have one, and we can't even finish off with this witness today. We can't bring him tomorrow again. You have five minutes left, and then Judge Harhoff would like to put a few questions to the witness. That will be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am sorry to press the matter. We actually only had one witness scheduled for today. There was supposed to be two hours on direct and two hours on cross-examination. I took 50 minutes on direct, and the Defence took, I believe, well over two hours, two and a half hours, perhaps more. I don't think it's fair that the Prosecution is prejudiced by that. We do have the time this week, and there are a number of important topics that I cannot cover in five minutes. I made no objection to the Defence having additional time, and I think we should be entitled to have another 15 minutes to cover the topics that need to be covered. It will not cause us any difficulty with the witnesses for the week. And I am sorry to press the matter, but I do think in this case it is only fair.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber has heard what you have said. You mentioned fairness and equity, and therefore we shall adjourn now and resume tomorrow. So we shall again discuss a matter which I discussed at the beginning of this hearing. Both parties should abide by the time that is being allocated; otherwise, we will be unable to finish within the time frame. The Court stands adjourned. And, Witness, we shall ask you to return tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
